summary: Use Node runtime interop for named ESM imports from CommonJS because names are heuristic static-analysis conveniences.

target.notes: Node can preconstruct named exports from static source analysis; they are not a general live view of later module.exports mutations.

semantics.liveness: later additions/updates are not generally reflected in named exports

caveats: Recognized CommonJS export patterns are Node/cjs-module-lexer version sensitive.
Default import is the reliable module.exports channel.

tests.name: detectable property may be named export
tests.input:
// a.cjs: exports.x=1
// main.mjs: import {x} from './a.cjs'; console.log(x);
tests.expected_behavior: prints 1 on Node profiles that detect the standard exports.x pattern

tests.name: default handles dynamic shape
tests.input:
// a.cjs: const k='x'; module.exports[k]=1
// main.mjs: import a from './a.cjs'; console.log(a.x);
tests.expected_behavior: default import reliably prints 1 even when named detection cannot infer x
